name: i-80 Gold Corp.

profile.description: i-80 Gold Corp. is a Reno, Nevada-based mining company exploring and advancing a portfolio of gold, silver, and polymetallic deposits across Nevada, including Ruby Hill, Granite Creek, and the Lone Tree autoclave refurbishment project. The company is in an aggressive multi-mine build-out phase — H1 2026 gold production rose to 22,000 ounces from 14,300 ounces a year earlier, with Q2 output of 11,098 oz up 166% YoY. CEO Richard Young (since September 2024) is targeting 50,000 oz in 2026 ramping to 150,000-200,000 oz/year by 2028 and 400,000-500,000 oz/year by the early 2030s, funded by a $465M cash position. Granite Creek is ahead of plan and Archimedes targets first gold in Q4 2026.

innovation.label: DEVELOPING
innovation.analysis: Track Record (2/3): i-80 Gold is executing a significant multi-asset development plan — ramping Granite Creek (ahead of plan), restarting Ruby Hill, and advancing Archimedes toward first gold in Q4 2026 — that opened new production streams and drove gold output up 166% YoY in Q2 2026 (11,098 oz vs. 4,178 oz) and H1 production up 54% (22,000 oz vs 14,300 oz) [1]. AI Deployment (0/2): No evidence of AI-powered exploration, geological modeling, or operational automation was found in company disclosures or earnings calls. Market Share (0/2): i-80 Gold remains a junior/mid-tier Nevada developer producing ~50K oz/year — no claim to category leadership in a global gold market producing 3,600+ tonnes annually. Product Pipeline (2/2): The company has named, quantified next-stage projects — Granite Creek open pit PEA showing after-tax NPV of $421M and 30% IRR at $2,175/oz gold, Lone Tree autoclave refurbishment study, and Archimedes targeting first gold Q4 2026 — providing exceptional development visibility [2]. R&D Intensity (0/1): No R&D-as-percent-of-revenue metric applicable; exploration expenditure is the industry equivalent but not benchmarked against peers.

inspiration.label: DEVELOPING
inspiration.analysis: Mission Floor (2/4): i-80 Gold's stated purpose of becoming 'Nevada's next leading mid-tier gold producer' underpinned by a 'people-centered culture' is clear about what the company is building but reads as standard growth-stage mining company positioning rather than a distinctive, differentiated cause. Community Impact (2/2): The company made a joint $300,000 donation with Franco-Nevada Corporation to support Eureka County's first licensed childcare facility near its Ruby Hill property — a specific, quantified, and distinctive community investment directly tied to the company's operational footprint [1]. The company also published an inaugural Sustainability Report ('Driving the Future') focused on environmental stewardship and community engagement in Nevada [3]. Employee Retention (1/2): Management emphasizes a 'safety-first culture' and 'people-centered culture where every employee can contribute meaningfully,' and promoted four senior technical personnel while hiring three new senior executives to reduce execution risk during the build-out phase [1][3]. No specific turnover or tenure data was found. Insider Buying (0/2): No evidence of meaningful net insider buying activity was identified in available research.

infrastructure.label: WEAK
infrastructure.analysis: Mechanically scored as a Growth stock on available metrics. D/E of 174.0% is well above the 70% target but inside the 300% floor, scoring 0.548 (1x weight) [4]. ROE of -71.7% and profit margin of -198.8% are both deeply negative and floor at 0.0 (2x and 1x weight respectively), reflecting a company in heavy development-stage capex mode — net loss widened to $52.5M in Q2 2026 from $30.2M a year earlier on higher pre-development, evaluation, and exploration spend [1]. Revenue growth YoY of -12.5% (Q2 2026 revenue of $24.3M vs. $27.8M in Q2 2025, driven by third-party processing delays at Granite Creek) scores 0.25 against the -20% floor (1x weight) [1]. Forward P/E, PEG, and 5-year revenue CAGR are unavailable and excluded. The stock clears the liquidity floor comfortably: ~9.6M average daily shares at $1.61 implies ~$15.4M in daily dollar volume. The $465M cash position provides substantial development runway despite the negative profitability metrics [1].

ai_resilience.label: LOW RISK
ai_resilience.analysis: AI Risk Protection (8/9): i-80 Gold's business is physical gold and silver extraction, processing, and mine development in Nevada — a capital-intensive, permit-intensive, and labor-intensive activity that AI cannot structurally displace [1]. Gold mining requires geological expertise, heavy equipment operation, chemical processing (autoclaves for refractory ore), and extensive regulatory permitting, none of which can be substituted by artificial intelligence. No analyst commentary was found suggesting AI poses substitution risk to mining production or reserves. AI may eventually enhance geological modeling and mine planning optimization, but these are incremental efficiency gains rather than existential threats. AI Opportunity (0/1): No quantified AI-driven revenue or cost-saving initiative was identified in company disclosures or earnings calls.

infinite_game.summary: i-80 Gold is a well-capitalized growth-stage miner pursuing an ambitious, fully-funded multi-asset development plan with clear production milestones and a strong management team. However, the evidence points to a commercially-framed 'leading mid-tier producer' ambition rather than a Sinek-style Just Cause — the company is building a gold mining business, not advancing a cause that transcends any single product or leader. The genuine community investment at Ruby Hill and the safety-first culture demonstrate some beyond-profit thinking, but this reads primarily as a well-capitalized growth story rather than a cause-driven enterprise built to endure beyond the current gold cycle.

just_cause.analysis: Just Cause (0/3): The company's articulated ambition — becoming 'Nevada's next leading mid-tier gold producer' — is a commercial growth target rather than a service-oriented cause that invites broader participation or describes a future state beyond making money [1][3]. While the company engages in community investment and environmental stewardship, these read as corporate responsibility rather than evidence of a purpose that would guide the company through a fundamental strategic dilemma. No formal mission or purpose statement beyond growth-focused positioning was found.

courage_to_lead.analysis: Courage to Lead (1/2): Management is continuing to fund an aggressive multi-mine development plan (Ruby Hill, Granite Creek, Archimedes, Lone Tree) even as net losses widened to $52.5M in Q2 2026 from $30.2M a year prior, choosing to prioritize long-term production capacity over near-term earnings — a real long-horizon bet backed by $465M cash [1]. CEO Young committed to a 50,000 oz target for 2026 ramping to 150,000-200,000 oz by 2028, demonstrating conviction in the development thesis despite mounting losses.

trusting_teams.analysis: Trusting Teams (1/2): The company emphasizes a 'safety-first culture' and a 'people-centered culture where every employee can contribute meaningfully' in sustainability materials, promoted four senior technical personnel internally, and hired three experienced senior executives to reduce execution risk during the build-out phase [1][3]. CEO Young's operational background (Barrick Gold's Goldstrike, Teranga Gold founder) brings credibility. No specific tenure, turnover, or empowerment data was found to justify a higher score.

existential_flexibility.analysis: Existential Flexibility (1/2): The company adopted a filtered tailings system offering a smaller environmental footprint and lower closure costs than conventional tailings storage, underwent a CEO transition from founder Ewan Downie to operationally-focused Richard Young in 2024, and pivoted from exploration-stage to active multi-mine development — incremental but meaningful operational and strategic evolution rather than a transformative reinvention [2][3].

worthy_rivals.analysis: Worthy Rivals (0/1): No evidence of collaborative or self-improvement-oriented competitive framing toward other Nevada gold producers was found in available management commentary. The company's competitive positioning focuses on its unique infrastructure (autoclave processing for refractory ore) rather than acknowledging and learning from peers' strengths.

investment_thesis: i-80 Gold is a well-capitalized Nevada gold developer ($465M cash) executing a multi-mine build-out that lifted H1 2026 gold production to 22,000 ounces from 14,300 ounces in H1 2025, with Q2 output up 166% YoY to 11,098 oz [1]. Granite Creek is running ahead of plan, Archimedes targets first gold in Q4 2026, and the Granite Creek open pit PEA shows an after-tax NPV of $421M and 30% IRR at $2,175/oz gold — economics that would be even stronger at current gold prices above $2,600/oz [2]. Management has laid out a credible ramp to 150,000-200,000 oz/year by 2028 and 400,000-500,000 oz/year by the early 2030s, leveraging Nevada's mining-friendly jurisdiction and i-80's rare autoclave processing capability for refractory ore. The $1.39B market cap suggests the market is beginning to price in the development trajectory. A filtered tailings system and the Franco-Nevada-backed Eureka County childcare facility signal a management team building durable community relationships as it scales [1][3].
thesis_continued: The bear case is grounded in current financial reality: profit margin of -198.8%, ROE of -71.7%, and a net loss widening to $52.5M in Q2 2026 (from $30.2M a year earlier) reflect a company still years from self-funding production economics, with Q2 revenue actually declining 12.5% YoY to $24.3M due to third-party processing bottlenecks at Granite Creek [1]. D/E of 174% is elevated, and despite the large $465M cash balance, operating cash flow of -$144M and free cash flow of -$114M TTM show the cash is being consumed by development capex at a substantial rate [4]. The development plan envisions building five mines simultaneously — Granite Creek, Ruby Hill, Archimedes, Lone Tree, and Granite Creek open pit — creating execution complexity and permitting risk across multiple sites in parallel. The mechanical Infrastructure score of 2/10 reflects a company whose investment case rests entirely on successful execution of the development plan rather than current financial durability, and gold price sensitivity means any sustained pullback below $2,000/oz would materially impair project economics.
key_catalysts: Archimedes achieving first gold production in Q4 2026 and Granite Creek continuing its ahead-of-plan ramp, demonstrating the multi-mine development strategy is converting from capex to production [1]
Lone Tree autoclave refurbishment advancing toward a construction decision, which would unlock refractory ore processing capacity rare in Nevada and drive a step-change in margins [2]
Granite Creek open pit project progressing toward construction on the back of a $421M after-tax NPV / 30% IRR PEA, with upside from current gold prices ($2,600+/oz) above the $2,175/oz base case [2]
key_risks: Persistent negative profitability (ROE -71.7%, profit margin -198.8%) and a widening net loss ($52.5M in Q2 2026) mean the company remains dependent on its cash balance — with -$144M TTM operating cash flow consuming the $465M position, runway extends approximately 3 years absent additional financing [1][4]

Simultaneous multi-mine development (five projects) creates execution complexity, and Nevada permitting requirements (air quality, mercury control, water pollution, reclamation) carry above-average timeline and regulatory risk for each individual project [2]
Revenue declined 12.5% YoY in Q2 2026 due to third-party processing delays at Granite Creek, highlighting the dependency on external infrastructure until the Lone Tree autoclave is operational [1]
